title: SEOstrich - GET FOUND.
pitch: SEO scares most businesses. SEOstrich builds your SEO strategy from measured data, then puts every decision on the page as WebMCP tools so your own AI assistant can audit, argue and further shape it.
about_excerpt: SEO scares most businesses. SEOstrich builds your SEO strategy from measured data, then puts every decision on the page as WebMCP tools so your own AI assistant can audit, argue and further shape it. Like Comment Story Updates SEOstrich banner 24 WebMCP tools - read-only, call DataForSEO, modify runs ChatGPT-created Content Calendar based on the SEO Strategy and AI Visibility reports ChatGPT using WebMCP tools for extra research - content brief for a post Chat-GPT using WebMCP to obtain data for visualization - pillar 1 Chat-GPT using WebMCP to obtain data for visualization - pillar 2 Chat-GPT using WebMCP to show the sweet spots in terms of volume and difficulty Inspiration For years I have treated SEO as something complicated, difficult and distant. It was only 7 months ago that I became fascinated with SEO. I had the opportunity to closely collaborate with a couple of strong SEO professionals at work and they inspired me to go deeper into the topic and to discover its richness. Still, most of my colleagues don't share my enthusiasm for SEO. Additionally, I've had the opportunity to discuss SEO in detail with a few SEO agencies and through those conversations I discovered that most small and medium businesses are scared of and confused by the topic of SEO - just as I was a few months ago. Others, even if they are interested in getting better at SEO, find the dedicated professional SEO tools unaffordable and never dig deeper. Those who do use the popular paid SEO tools are drowning in enormous tables and sheets with keywords that they share back and forth with colleagues and clients. At the same time, there are affordable, high quality data sources, such as DataForSEO. If only someone integrated with them, made sense of all of the endpoints that they offer and mapped those to client needs in an elegant way... But that won't fully remove the barrier to the topic of SEO for everybody. So when I heard about the WebMCP hackathon I saw an opportunity to expose as WebMCP tools the key steps in a few SEO workflows. This way, essentially giving easy access to all of the SEO data that people are drowning in or confused by. And then a user could open ChatGPT and suddenly make sense of it all by asking a couple of questions in chat. WebMCP is a real opportunity to make the SEO topic accessible to so many small and medium businesses and help them get found in a world that is increasingly drowning in data and slop. What it does SEOstrich enables you to collaborate with an AI Assistant to make sense of complex detailed SEO analyses (SEO content opportunities, AI visibility reports). This way human + agent co-design an SEO strategy that helps their websites get found. WebMCP enables a person to use the outputs of a few SEO AI Agents, analyze them, edit and shape them in collaboration with their own AI Assistant so that the final strategy is tailored precisely to the given business's needs and goals. Examples of what people and agents could do together: take the SEO content strategy and the AI visibility reports generated for a given business. Use the WebMCP tools to construct a detailed content calendar for the next three weeks - one long-form post targeting organic SEO and two shorter posts aimed at increasing AI citations. For each post pick the primary keyword from the given content pillar and enrich that with a few secondary keywords, essentially calling the DataForSEO data source. Then recommend the structure of each post. The human then writes the posts themselves to make it sound genuine and avoid it being perceived like another piece of slop on the internet. In other words, even though I haven't built the content calendar functionality exactly as a set of users need it and there are no post briefs yet, the users' agents have all the necessary tools to generate a calendar according to the cadence and requirements of their own business the SEOstrich agent has recommended 3 to 4 pillars of the content strategy (main themes to write about over time) - based on the initial brief and subsequent keyword analysis. However, one of the pillars doesn't resonate with the user, one of the discarded clusters is actually good in their opinion and there is a missing part of the brief that deserves a dedicated pillar in the content strategy. The human explains that to their own agent, which can further analyze in detail the existing clusters, can perform extra searches against the DataForSEO data source and give a recommendation. The fully WebMCP enabled system allows the agent to reach conclusions such as: "fine we can drop that cluster that you didn't relate with, but the discarded cluster should remain discarded as there is barely any demand for it and creating content on those topics is a waste of time. However, your new addition to the brief makes total sense, it comes with a lot of demand and the topics are genuinely in line with your interests." The above is a significant improvement in the usability of SEO research and analyses. While users still have access to all of the SEO data, they don't have to get lost in countless spreadsheets, filters, tabs, etc. Instead, it is enough to communicate their intent to their own agent. By exposing a rich set of read and write WebMCP tools, SEOstrich enables users' agents to shape analyses and strategies exactly as per their users' intent - without being limited by specific workflows that have been built or missing functionalities. The goal is one - SEO shouldn't be something distant and confusing - it should be just a tool that anybody could use to help make their business get found. How we built it The stack includes a Next.js frontend, hosted on Vercel, that registers 23 tools on document.modelContext, and a FastAPI backend that runs on Railway. Both SEO flows (content strategy and AI visibility) run as fixed code graphs where the order and gates are set in code, while the models reason about the data, decide grouping and wording. DataForSEO is used as the source of keyword insights such as term difficulty, demand, what your competitors already rank for, what people actually ask in ChatGPT and Google AI. There is per-run locking and append-only history for each generated SEO report, so that several judges can edit the same report safely. There is also an option to restore the defaults of seeded reports. The baseline project that I started with had a broken single-turn orchestrator, poor limited UI, no status streaming, no WebMCP support, no graphs for the critical parts of the SEO workflows, wasn't hosted anywhere, had drained my DataForSEO account a couple of times due to inefficient wiring. It had a half-working POC memory system that made matters even more complicated. The memory module has been fully unplugged, to allow for clear focus on the SEO + WebMCP theme.
